title: NHC's 2025 season verification: Google DeepMind ensemble mean outperformed official short-range Atlantic track forecasts in NHC's first operational use of AI models
summary: In 2025, its first season with AI models in operations, the US National Hurricane Center found that Google DeepMind's ensemble mean beat its official Atlantic track forecasts at 12 to 72 hours.
account: James Franklin, a former branch chief at the US National Hurricane Center (NHC), shared his own verification of the 2025 season in late October 2025. Michael Lowry relayed it on 3 November 2025, and CNN reported it on 3 December 2025. Franklin found that the DeepMind ensemble was the most accurate track and intensity guidance of the 2025 season. CNN added that it did not perform evenly with each storm. NHC's Forecast Verification Report for the 2025 season is dated 30 March 2026. It states that 2025 marked the first time that NHC incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations. In the Atlantic track comparison, the Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) slightly outperformed the official forecast at lead times from 12 to 72 hours. Official forecasts outperformed the consensus aids TVCA, HCCA and FSSE. In the eastern North Pacific, GDMI performed considerably better than every other individual model. It beat the official forecast and all consensus aids at 48 to 120 hours. For intensity it was the top individual model from 12 to 48 hours. GDMI was not available early in the season, so the first storms are excluded from these comparisons. On 10 September 2026 Lowry reported that Franklin's numbers showed DeepMind ahead of NHC's official track forecasts for a second year.
purpose: Google DeepMind's experimental model gives National Hurricane Center forecasters ensemble guidance on the track and intensity of tropical cyclones.
system: Google DeepMind AI hurricane forecast model, ensemble mean designated GDMI in NHC guidance

fields.summary: In 2025, its first season with AI models in operations, the US National Hurricane Center found that Google DeepMind's ensemble mean beat its official Atlantic track forecasts at 12 to 72 hours.
fields.account: James Franklin, a former branch chief at the US National Hurricane Center (NHC), shared his own verification of the 2025 season in late October 2025. Michael Lowry relayed it on 3 November 2025, and CNN reported it on 3 December 2025. Franklin found that the DeepMind ensemble was the most accurate track and intensity guidance of the 2025 season. CNN added that it did not perform evenly with each storm. NHC's Forecast Verification Report for the 2025 season is dated 30 March 2026. It states that 2025 marked the first time that NHC incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations. In the Atlantic track comparison, the Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) slightly outperformed the official forecast at lead times from 12 to 72 hours. Official forecasts outperformed the consensus aids TVCA, HCCA and FSSE. In the eastern North Pacific, GDMI performed considerably better than every other individual model. It beat the official forecast and all consensus aids at 48 to 120 hours. For intensity it was the top individual model from 12 to 48 hours. GDMI was not available early in the season, so the first storms are excluded from these comparisons. On 10 September 2026 Lowry reported that Franklin's numbers showed DeepMind ahead of NHC's official track forecasts for a second year.
